title: Towards Reconstructing Geographically Diverse Architecture with 3D Foundation Models
claim: A benchmark spans many geographically diverse landmarks across world regions, each with dense ground-truth reconstructions and regional metadata.
layout: Single world map, color-coded regions, callout cards with leader lines to locations
description: A pale world map on a blue ellipse background. Colored dots mark the locations of the benchmark's landmarks, with color set by region: North America, Latin America, Europe, Africa, West/Central Asia, South Asia, East Asia and Southeast Asia. About 20 white callout cards surround the map. Thick colored leader lines join each card to its location. Each card has a region label with a colored dot at the top. Below the label is a dense point-cloud reconstruction of a landmark, such as Chichen Itza, Gouda City Hall, Taipei 101 or Prambanan Temple. A small human silhouette gives scale. The landmark name is at the bottom of the card. Card sizes vary. The large reconstructions, such as Taipei 101 and Chichen Itza, draw the eye first. Dots clustered in Europe and North America show uneven density.
caption: ArchWorld. We present a geographically diverse benchmark of 396 in-the-wild 3D landmarks (92K images) across eight geographic regions with rich metadata and metric-scale dense ground-truth reconstructions, enabling evaluation of 3D foundation models disaggregated by region.
abstract: Internet-scale photo collections of real-world landmarks have driven progress in 3D computer vision yet remain highly challenging for modern 3D foundation models (3DFMs) that estimate scene structure in a single feed-forward pass. In this work, we introduce ArchWorld, a benchmark of 3D architectural landmarks with high geographic coverage and rich metadata. We use this benchmark to conduct a thorough error analysis of current 3DFMs to understand where they fall short and how they can be improved. We examine socially relevant disparities in model error and find that model performance varies by geographic region; however, unlike typical fairness regimes, the trends only partially match training data representation. Our investigation reveals that the observed geographic disparities reflect not only differences in data representation and scene size but also differences in region-specific architectural features and background distractors that make scenes from different regions inherently vary in difficulty. Leveraging insights from these model failings, we introduce an intervention scheme that improves 3DFM performance while simultaneously reducing geographic disparities.
